title: Caller-selected CTA width recurs in RMSNorm gradient and SwiGLU; expose a guarded explicit candidate rewrite

evidence.note: Turn 2 confirmation records correctness and stable timing: 2.432 us candidate versus 3.040 us baseline, 10/10 pair wins. Candidate declares 16 warps. Run later fails at turn 4 for missing structured terminal; the local confirmation remains evidence, not Run promotion.
Terminal-best confirmation: 2.144 us candidate versus 3.488 us baseline, with a 16-warp role. This is an independent pointwise family, not a second copy of RMSNorm.

observation: Single-role pure tensor Triton programs map the role width to num_warps. Caller-chosen width changes SDK resource/layout choices while preserving the operation/access graph. A previous missing power-of-two preflight allowed a six-warp RMSNorm candidate to crash the SDK; the current integration also needs that guarded refusal before SDK entry.
proposed_change: Add explicit specialize_triton_warps using existing SpecializationResult and whole-candidate reassessment. Match only the documented bounded operation/ownership domain, preserve ABI and metadata, reject invalid or excessive widths before allocation, and keep the measured choice in Lab. No implicit tuning, no bitwise-equivalence or universal-speedup promise.
verification_plan: Independent source review and full Corpus Gate; public positive/negative tests including a held-out family. On the successor, evaluate current width-1 floor and pass-produced width-8/16 candidates for RMSNorm gradient and SwiGLU against the same old fixed baselines, with five-case correctness, stable paired timing and NCU. Retain null/negative transfer and original failed Run states.
